title: Normalized ordinary differential and tensor-pullback presentations on the etale site
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], use the sheaf of rings $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ and the log-differential structure ring of [def-per-log-differential-symbol-sheaf], and its module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $f:X\to S$, a normalized ordinary differential presentation consists of a module sheaf $E$, an isomorphism of its additive presheaf with the tensor-section presheaf of the existing $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], and a universal relative derivation $d:\mathcal O_X\to E$. Relative derivations are additive, satisfy Leibniz and restrictions, and annihilate functions from $S$ on every relative etale diagram. Universality means that each such derivation into any module sheaf $T$ factors uniquely through a module map $E\to T$. For $c:Z\to W$ and module sheaves $E$ on $W$ and $F$ on $Z$, a relative module map is a family of additive maps $E(U)\to F(V)$ for all etale $U\to W$, $V\to Z$ and $k:V\to U$ over $c$, semilinear over $k^\sharp$ and natural in both test objects. A tensor-pullback presentation of $E$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is a module sheaf $P$ on $Z$ and such a relative map $\eta:E\to P$ through which every relative module map $E\to T$ factors uniquely as a module map $P\to T$. Thus it is the unit-normalized representing pair for $\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{c^{-1}\mathcal O_W}c^{-1}E$, not an uncharacterized isomorphic module. These are interfaces specifying representing pairs, with no object chosen from a mere existence assertion.
